title: Production Deployment
outcome: Deploy the real topology—Next.js, NestJS image, Supabase services, migrations, domains/TLS/CORS, secrets, health checks, smoke tests, and rollback—as one release system.
artifact: Staging and production deployment runbooks with release identity, environment matrix, smoke tests, and rollback procedure.
labSteps: Create separate staging/production environment matrices before entering any dashboard values.
Deploy Next.js from the intended monorepo root with public/server env vars separated.
Deploy the exact API container artifact and verify bind address, PORT, and readiness endpoint.
Apply database migrations as a controlled release step and document backward-compatibility assumptions.
Configure custom domains/TLS and the exact CORS/redirect origins for production.
Run a smoke-test checklist and practice rollback of code while reasoning about whether the database migration is reversible.
failureModes: Preview deployment points to production database
Secrets copied into source or image
Code deploy occurs before required migration or vice versa without compatibility plan
Rollback plan assumes schema can always be downgraded
mastery: Can explain code vs database rollback constraints
principles: Production deployment is a system of frontend, API, database, DNS, secrets, migrations, and observability rather than one deploy button.
Apply database migrations in a controlled step before code depends on the new schema.
Use environment-specific configuration while keeping the same tested application artifact where possible.
Plan smoke tests and rollback before release so recovery is part of deployment design.
